questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy if you are willing to pay. However, student accommodation is much more expensive and I didn't even considered it for a second.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Find your accommodation when you ARE in Melbourne. Don't try to sort it out before you arrive, it is very hard as they want you to inspect the apartment physically. Arrive in Melbourne in advance in a hotel/airbnb and attend inspections

questions.answer: Took four subjects on my fifth semester. Three courses on year 2/3 and 1 on year 1

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Requires more participation in classes. Hurdle requirements in most of the subjects e.g, you need to attend 10 out of 12 classes to pass. However, there are no end of semester examination in most of the subject. Your grade are a combination of attending, participation, assignments etc and in some cases a end of semester examination. All with a different weighting on the final grade. E.g, attending 10/12 classes 10%, first assignment 10%, second assignment 20% and examination 60%.

questions.answer: If you are in Melbourne, go to the Grampians to see some wildlife and nature. Don't rush to leave Melbourne every time you got some days off or in the weekend. Prioritise to stay in Melbourne and explore the city in (some) weekends.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1 Don't try to find your accommodation before you arrive in Melbourne. Stay at a cheap hotel or an airbnb for the first week or two and search for accommodation when you get here! Much easier! 

2 Take subjects that are relevant for your future or current studies (or you find interesting). 

3 Don't be in a hurry to leave Melbourne and its surroundings for Sydney or the east coast on weekends and holidays. Melbourne is the coolest and best city in Australia (the Aussies will say the same) and Victoria is fantastic. Find the balance between exploring Melbourne/Victoria and the rest of Australia (Big country, you cannot explore every part of Australia)

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: IF YOU ARRIVE IN JULY, DON'T GET SCARED OR DISAPPOINTED BY THE WEATHER. Melbourne is windy and pretty cold in July (feels like October/March in Denmark). You will miss the Danish summer when its warmer in Denmark than Melbourne in July and August. But i'm telling you, it's getting seriously hot FR!! The weather will change from September, just hang in. Melbourne is very sunny even in the cooler months. In November and December some days will exceed 35 degrees.
